message.content:
Sky‑blue is one of those classic hues that shows up in many design systems. In Pantone’s catalog there isn’t a single “official” code because the exact tone you’re after (lightness, saturation, etc.) matters—but here are a few widely used references:

| Context | Typical Pantone Code |
|---------|----------------------|
| **Light, airy sky‑blue** – often seen in fashion & interior palettes | **Pantone 290 C** (a very pale, almost pastel blue) |
| **Bright, vibrant sky‑blue** – popular in branding & print | **Pantone 298 C** (clear, vivid blue) |
| **Soft, muted sky‑blue** – good for corporate stationery & subtle backgrounds | **Pantone 292 C** |

If you have a particular application in mind—like digital vs. print, matte vs. gloss—you may want to double‑check against your own swatch book or a physical Pantone guide. For most general purposes, Pantone 290 C will give you that quintessential light sky hue.
